messages:
arjun: Heads up — since last night we've got a bunch of nodes sitting at ~12-18% GPU util while other nodes are saturated. cost spike noticed and a few small jobs got preempted when we tried to binpack.

melissa: saw that too. any recent changes to podAntiAffinity or the tiny gpu class?

kai: not that I pushed. kube-scheduler logs show a lot of pods with RequiredDuringScheduling podAntiAffinity on `ml-role=worker-small`. They end up spread across hosts (node islands) instead of being packed. snippet from scheduler logs: 
```
I0321 22:10:11.123456 1 scheduler_predicates.go:123] Pod "train-abc" fails PodAffinityRules: requiredDuringScheduling: podAntiAffinity topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
```

melissa: that policy makes sense for noisy single-GPU training, but for tiny inference/experiments it's hurting density.

arjun: also noticed NIC Tx spikes when we forcibly consolidate — when we pack 6 small GPU pods onto one node the NIC saturates and latency spikes. `node-network-bw` metric: 
```
node/eu-west1-gpu-01 network_tx_percent=92
```

kai: so two orthogonal problems: affinity-induced spreading + network saturation when overpacking.

taylor: options: (1) change small-pod class to preferredDuringScheduling (soft) instead of required, (2) create a dedicated compact pool (label + taint) for <0.5 GPU requests and move them there, (3) tune descheduler low-node-utilization thresholds to rebin at offpeak, (4) add a simple network-aware admission/scheduler plugin that caps pods-per-nic.

melissa: I like the compact-pool + taint approach — low-risk, canaryable. admission webhook can default-place small requests there.

ops-bot: :warning: Fragmentation alert: GPU fragment index increased +18% in prod between 22:00-02:00 UTC. High spread across eu-west1 cluster.

arjun: proposal for canary: label 10 nodes in eu-west1 as `compact=true`, taint `compact=true:NoSchedule`, create a `small-gpu` nodeSelector in our tiny-runner Helm chart (and add toleration). Run for 48h, measure token cost/per-util and NIC usage.

kai: add a limitRange or mutating webhook to enforce max pods-per-nic on those nodes — or at least expose that metric so we don't oversubscribe NIC. I can wire a node-exporter dashboard to alert at 75% NIC util.

melissa: also let's temporarily relax podAntiAffinity on the small runner chart: change required -> preferred with weight 100. That keeps some spreading but allows packing.

taylor: agree. action items: arjun: roll the 10-node canary + Helm change; melissa: PR to chart to change anti-affinity to preferred; kai: dashboard & mutating webhook prototype; I'll own gating and metrics collection.

arjun: starting infra changes now — will post deploy cmds and a quick check command.

melissa: :thumbsup: ping if you need node images or extra quotas.

kai: FYI, when we pack more, watch for RDMA/IB fallback — some instance types lose NIC offload when many vNICs are in play. Good to test at 4, 6, 8 pods/node.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Canary plan created: milestone "compact-pool-canary" assigned to arjun, kai, melissa.

arjun: I'll post a short runbook + commands in ~30m. If metrics look good after 24h we flip more nodes.

taylor: sg. if the network-aware plugin looks hairy we can start with the compact pool + descheduler and iterate.

arjun: noted. thanks everyone — will update thread with timestamps for the canary steps and the runbook once infra changes are up.
